input.question: Just how different are the male and female brain?
input.ground_truth: There was a [thread](_URL_0_) earlier today in /r/AskScienceDiscussion about the brains of transgender men and women. You should give it a look, it has some interesting results about gender and brain morphology. It turns out the brains of transgender men and women most closely resemble the brains of the gender they identify with, not the sex they were born with. It also has some links to some of the primary literature about the sex differences in brain morphology. Should give you a good idea about how different the brains of men and women are.

Question: Just how different are the male and female brain?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your brain is like a big toy box. Boys and girls both have toy boxes, but sometimes the toys inside are arranged a little bit differently.

Some people say that boys’ toy boxes might have more cars and blocks, while girls’ toy boxes might have more dolls and dresses. But it’s not like every boy’s toy box is exactly the same, and every girl’s toy box is exactly the same!

Most of the toys (which are like the parts of the brain that help you think, feel, and do things) are the same in every toy box. But sometimes, the way the toys are organized or used can be a little different for boys and girls. This is because of things like how we grow up, what we like to play with, and the things we learn from our families and friends.

So, our brains are a lot alike, but also a little bit different, just like how every person is special in their own way!
